channel.title: Jiǎoluò Shūwū · 角落書屋
channel.description: A reading nook for Chinese language and civilisation. Characters, vocabulary, grammar, history, philosophy, and the world they shaped.

item.title: 朝 · dynasty, imperial court, to face toward; (zhāo) morning
item.description: The sun rising among grasses with the moon still in the sky. From that dawn scene grow two readings: zhāo, the morning and its youthful vigor, and cháo, the court that met at daybreak, the dynasty it served, and the preposition toward.

item.title: 城 · city, city wall, town
item.description: A rampart of earth raised around a settlement: the character where the wall and the city it protects are one and the same word.

item.title: 传 · to pass on, transmit, spread; (zhuan) a biography, a commentary
item.description: The person radical carrying something onward: one figure handing a thing to the next. From that image grow the senses of 传, read chuan when it means to pass down, transmit, and spread, and read zhuan when it names a biography or a classical commentary.

item.title: 代 · generation, era, to substitute, on behalf of
item.description: The person radical carrying the sense of succession: one figure standing in the place of another. From that single image grow the four faces of 代: to replace or act for someone, to do a thing on their behalf, the generation that succeeds the one before, and the era or dynasty in which a life is set.

item.title: 调 · (diào) to transfer, tune, accent; (tiáo) to adjust, to blend, to mediate
item.description: A high-frequency polyphone with two readings. As diào it means to transfer, a melody or key, a tone, an accent; as tiáo it means to adjust, to blend, to mediate. The reading tells you whether 调 is moving things or harmonizing them.

item.title: 夫 · husband, a grown man, laborer; the literary particle fú
item.description: A grown man pictured with a hairpin marking adulthood: the husband and the married couple (丈夫 夫妻 夫人 夫妇), the adult man and laborer (农夫 渔夫 大夫), skill and effort (功夫 工夫), and the classical literary particle 夫 fú that opens a sentence.

item.title: 功 · merit, achievement, skill, effort
item.description: Merit earned through effort: from meritorious service and success to the patient skill the Chinese call gongfu, and even work in physics.

item.title: 古 · ancient, old, classical
item.description: The mouth radical holding what ten generations have spoken down the years: 古 is what is old because it has been handed on. From that single image grow the senses of antiquity (古代 古老 远古), the classical and the antique (古典 古文 古董 古迹 考古), and the quaint or unconventional (古怪 古板).

item.title: 化 · to change, to transform, to melt
item.description: The character of transformation itself: melting, digesting, civilizing, and the productive -ize suffix that builds half of modern technical Chinese.

item.title: 解 · to untie, to solve, to explain, to dissolve
item.description: The character for cutting apart and undoing: untying and liberating, solving and explaining, dissolving and relieving. A polyphone read jiě, jiè, and xiè, pictured as a hand prying an ox horn from the ox.

item.title: 历 · to experience, history, calendar
item.description: One simplified glyph that absorbed two traditional characters: 歷 (to pass through, history) and 曆 (calendar). The word that holds both lived experience and reckoned time.

item.title: 连 · to link, to join, even
item.description: Carts moving in a line: a character that joins things in space, in sequence, and in emphasis, from 连接 to the famous 连...都 construction.

item.title: 民 · the people, a citizen, folk
item.description: The common people as a collective subject: the populace, the citizen, the folk and the nation, and the civilian set against the military. From 人民 the people to 民族 ethnic nation to 民主 democracy.

item.title: 容 · to contain, to allow, appearance
item.description: A roof over a valley: the space that holds. To contain, to tolerate, the face one shows, and the easy in rongyi.

item.title: 社 · society, an association, the god of the soil
item.description: The altar radical beside the earth: a shrine to the god of the soil and the community that gathered around it. From that image grow society itself, the many kinds of association and agency, and the ancient soil-and-grain spirits that once stood for the state.

item.title: 世 · world, age, generation, lifetime
item.description: A pictograph traditionally read as three tens joined together, the span of thirty years that makes one generation. From that root grow the four faces of 世: the generation that succeeds the one before, the lifetime or the life to come, the era stacked from many lives, and the wider world of human society in which all of it unfolds.

item.title: 首 · head, first, chief, a measure word for songs and poems
item.description: A drawn head, with hair above an eye, and from it the senses of first, foremost, chief, leader, and the classifier you count songs and poems with. 首 is its own radical.

item.title: 望 · to gaze afar, to hope, reputation
item.description: A person on a mound looking into the distance, with the moon above: from that raised gaze grow three senses. To gaze and look afar (眺望, 望远镜, 张望), to hope and expect (希望, 期望, 盼望, 失望), and reputation or prestige (名望, 威望, 声望). As a coverb it can even mean toward, like 朝 or 向.

item.title: 武 · martial, military, valiant
item.description: The foot radical 止 carrying a dagger-axe 戈: the soldier on the march, and the older reading that to wield arms well is finally to halt them. From 武力 armed force to 武术 martial arts to 威武 powerful and dignified, the character holds the whole world of strength wielded with discipline.

item.title: 形 · shape, form, to appear, to compare
item.description: The character for visible form: shape and figure, the body as form, the act of taking shape and being described, and the lay of a situation. A pictophonetic compound built on the pattern-strokes radical 彡.

item.title: 性 · nature, character, sex/gender, the -ness/-ity suffix
item.description: The heart radical carrying the sense of innate nature: what a thing is born to be. From that core grow the four faces of 性: a persons disposition or character, sex and gender, the property or quality of a thing, and the productive abstract suffix that turns adjectives into -ness and -ity nouns.

item.title: 楚辞 · Songs of Chu
item.description: The shamanistic southern voice that gave Chinese literature its second pole: visionary, romantic, and inconsolably exiled.

item.title: 古琴 · the scholar's zither
item.description: The seven-string zither Confucius played throughout his life, and the origin of 知音, the word for a person who truly understands you.

item.title: 生旦净末丑 · Role Types in Peking Opera
item.description: Five role categories, each a complete performance tradition -- voice, movement, makeup, and costume as a total semiotic system.

item.title: 鲁迅 · Lu Xun
item.description: The writer who looked at traditional Chinese society and saw cannibalism, and the complicated, unresolvable legacy he left behind.

item.title: 山水画 · landscape painting
item.description: Chinese landscape painting encodes a theory in its name: 山 (mountain, yang, permanent) and 水 (water, yin, changing) in dynamic tension. A space to inhabit in the imagination, not a view to frame.

item.title: 诗经 · Book of Songs
item.description: China oldest poetry anthology: three hundred poems that Confucius said no educated person could afford to ignore.

item.title: 书法风格 · The Five Scripts of Chinese Calligraphy
item.description: Five script styles chart two thousand years of Chinese writing, from the solemn bronze inscriptions of the Zhou to the explosive cursive of the Tang masters.

item.title: 水墨画 · Ink-Wash Painting
item.description: Where the brush meets philosophy: five tones of ink, the art of leaving space, and landscapes that are not about landscape at all.

item.title: 宋词 · Song Dynasty Lyric
item.description: The poem that sings: fixed tune patterns, named meters, and three masters who defined what the Chinese lyric could feel.
